corporation; or 
 
(iv) any law enforcement organization including the police or any central or state revenue 
authorities; or 
(v) a public prosecutor in connection with any criminal proceedings. 
 
Provided that sharing of information shall be in accordance with such assurances of

confidentiality as the Board determines appropriate. 
Explanation - Nothing in these regulations is intended to limit, or shall be construed to limit, the 
ability of the public prosecutor to share such evidence with potential witnesses or accused in 
connection with any criminal proceedings. 
 
(3) The Original Information and identity provided by an Informant shall be held in confidence 
and exempted from disclosure under clauses (g) and (h) of sub-section (1) of section 8 of the 
Right to Information Act, 2005 (No. 22 of 2005). 
 
(4) Subject to the law of evidence for the time being in force, nothing in these regulations shall 
prejudice the right of the Board to use or to rely on information received otherwise. 
 
(5) No person shall have the right to compel disclosure of the identity, existence of an Informant 
or the information provided by an Informant, except to the extent relied upon in any proceeding 
initiated against such person by the Board. 
Explanation 1 . – The confidentiality in respect of the identity and existence of the Informant 
shall be maintained throughout the process of investigation, inquiry and examination as well as 
during any proceedings before the Board and save where the evidence of the Informant is 
required during such proceedings, advance notice of such evidence may be provided to the 
noticee at least seven (7) working days prior to the date of the scheduled hearing for evidence. 
Explanation 2 . – In proceedings before any authority other than the Board, the Board may 
request maintenance of confidentiality of the identity and existence of an Informant in such 
proceeding. 
 
 
Protection against retaliation and victimisation 
 
7I. (1) Every person required to have a Code of Conduct under these regulations shall ensure that

such a Code of Conduct provides for suitable protection against any discharge, termination, 
demotion, suspension, threats, harassment, directly or indirectly or discrimination against any 
employee who files a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form, irrespective of whether the 
information is considered or rejected by the Board or he or she is eligible for a Reward under 
these regulations, by reason of: 
(i) filing a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form under these regulations; 
(ii) testifying in, participating in, or otherwise assisting or aiding the Board in any 
investigation, inquiry, audit, examination or proceeding instituted or about to be instituted 
for an alleged violation of insider trading laws or in any manner aiding the enforcement 
action taken by the Board; or 
(iii) breaching any confidentiality agreement or provisions of any terms and conditions of 
employment or engagement solely to prevent any employee from cooperating with the 
Board in any manner. 
Explanation 1. - For the purpose of this Chapter, "employee" means any individual who during 
employment may become privy to information relating to violation of insider trading laws and 
files a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form under these regulations and is a director, partner, 
regular or contractual employee, but does not include an advocate. 
Explanation 2. - Nothing in this regulation shall require the employee to establish that,- 
(i) the Board has taken up any enforcement action in furtherance of information provided by 
such person; or 
(ii) the information provided fulfils the criteria of being considered as an Original 
Information under these regulations. 
 
(2) Nothing in these regulations shall prohibit any Informant who believes that he or she has

been subject to retaliation or victimisation by his or her employer, from approaching the 
competent court or tribunal for appropriate relief. 
 
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (2), any employer who violates this 
Chapter may be liable for penalty, debarment, suspension, and/or criminal prosecution by the 
Board, as the case may be: 
 
Provided that nothing in these regulations will require the Board to direct re-instatement or 
compensation by an employer. 
 
(4) Nothing in these regulations shall diminish the rights and privileges of or remedies available 
to any Informant under any other law in force. 
 
Void Agreements 
7J. (1) Any term in an agreement (oral or written) or Code of Conduct, is void in so far as it 
purports to preclude any person, other than an advocate, from submitting to the Board 
information relating to the violation of the securities laws that has occurred, is occurring or has a 
reasonable belief that it would occur. 
 
(2) No person shall by way of any threat or act impede an individual from communicating with 
the Board, including enforcing or threatening to enforce, a confidentiality agreement (other than 
agreements related to legal representations of a client and communications there under) with 
respect to such communications. 
Explanation. - No employer shall require an employee to notify him of any Voluntary 
Information Disclosure Form filed with the Board or to seek its prior permission or consent or 
guidance of any person engaged by the employer before or after such filing. 
 
No Amnesty 
7K. (1) Nothing in these regulations shall be deemed to provide any amnesty or immunity to an 
Informant for violation of securities law.

(2) Where an action against an Informant is deemed appropriate the Board may take into account 
the co-operation rendered in the final determination of any penalty, sanction, direction or 
settlement thereof, as the case may be. 
 
(3) Where an action against an Informant is deemed appropriate, the Board while determining 
the value of monetary sanctions shall not take into account the monetary sanctions that the 
Informant is ordered to pay or that which any other person is ordered to pay if the liability of 
 
such other person is based substantially on the conduct that the Informant directed, planned, or 
initiated. 
 
(4) An Informant who may be liable for enforcement action by the Board based on his or her 
conduct in connection with securities laws violations reported in the Voluntary Information 
Disclosure Form filed with the Board, may simultaneously or at any time thereafter file an 
application seeking settlement with confidentiality under Chapter IX of the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Settlement Proceedings) Regulations, 2018. 
 
(5) Notwithstanding any action taken by the Board against an Informant, the Informant may, 
after payment of any monetary amounts be eligible for a Reward. 
 
Functions of Informant Incentive Committee 
7L. (1) The Informant Incentive Committee shall be assisted by the Office of Informant 
Protection. 
 
(2) The Informant Incentive Committee shall give its recommendations to the Board on the 
following matters,- 
i. Eligibility of Informant for reward; 
ii. Determination under regulations 7E and 7G; and 
iii. Such other issues relating to Informant as the Board may require from time to time. 
 
(3) The Informant Incentive Committee shall conduct its meetings in the manner specified by the 
Board in this regard.

Public dissemination and incentivisation of Informant. 
7M. (1) The Board shall upload on its website the following,- 
i. Annual report of the Office of Informant Protection; 
ii. Press release informing the public that an intimation to the Informant has been issued 
under Regulation 7D; 
 
iii. Press release informing the public that a Reward has been paid under these 
regulations and the amount of Monetary Sanctions recovered pursuant to the 
information provided by the Informant; 
iv. The Order issuing the Reward; 
Explanation. – Nothing in this regulation shall require the Board to disclose information 
that could identify the Informant or the information provided by the Informant.]

SCHEDULE A

Principles of Fair Disclosure for purposes of Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair 
Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information

1. Prompt public disclosure of unpublished price sensitive information that would impact 
price discovery no sooner than credible and concrete information comes into being in order to 
make such information generally available.

2. Uniform and universal dissemination of unpublished price sensitive unpublished price 
sensitive information to avoid selective disclosure.

3. Designation of a senior officer as a chief investor relations officer to deal with 
dissemination of information and disclosure of unpublished price sensitive information.

4. Prompt dissemination of unpublished price sensitive information that gets disclosed 
selectively, inadvertently or otherwise to make such information generally available.

5. Appropriate and fair response to queries on news reports and requests for verification of 
market rumours by regulatory authorities.

6. Ensuring that information shared with analysts and research personnel is not unpublished 
price sensitive information.

7. Developing best practices to make transcripts or records of proceedings of meetings with 
analysts and other investor relations conferences on the official website to ensure official 
confirmation and documentation of disclosures made.

8. Handling of all unpublished price sensitive information on a need-to-know basis.

FACTUALIS BANK LIMITED (FICTIONAL ENTITY - HACKATHON DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT)
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: WIRE TRANSFERS AND SANCTIONS SCREENING
Document ID: FB-AML-WIRE-SOP | Version 4.1 | Effective date: 01 April 2026
Owner: Financial Crime Compliance Department | Approved by: Board Risk Committee

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This SOP sets out the controls the Bank applies to domestic and cross-border wire transfers originated or received by Factualis Bank Limited, and to the screening of such transfers against sanctions lists.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.2 This SOP applies to NEFT, RTGS and IMPS transfers, and to outward and inward cross-border remittances processed through the Bank's Treasury Operations unit.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.3 This SOP does not apply to correspondent banking relationships, virtual digital asset transfers, card network settlements, or trade finance transactions such as letters of credit. These are governed by separate policies that are not part of this SOP.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.4 Where this SOP is stricter than any applicable regulation, the stricter requirement of this SOP shall prevail.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Head of Financial Crime Compliance" or "HFCC" means the officer designated by the Board to head the Financial Crime Compliance Department.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.2 "Principal Officer" means the officer designated by the Bank under the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 for furnishing information to FIU-IND.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.3 "New Relationship Customer" means a customer whose first account with the Bank was opened less than 180 days before the date of the transfer.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.4 "Internal Watchlist" or "IWL" means the list of names maintained by the Financial Crime Compliance Department on the basis of past alerts, law enforcement requests and adverse media.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.5 "Working hours" means 09:30 to 17:30 IST on a day on which the Bank's head office is open for business.

3. ORIGINATOR AND BENEFICIARY INFORMATION
3.1 Every domestic wire transfer shall carry the name, account number and IFSC of both the originator and the beneficiary.

3. ORIGINATOR AND BENEFICIARY INFORMATION
3.2 Every cross-border wire transfer of Rs. 25,000 and above, or its equivalent in foreign currency, shall additionally carry the originator's address, date of birth and the purpose code of the remittance.

3. ORIGINATOR AND BENEFICIARY INFORMATION
3.3 A cross-border wire transfer that is received without complete originator information shall be placed on hold, and the remitting bank shall be asked to supply the missing information within 3 working days. If the information is not received within that period, the transfer shall be returned to the remitting bank.

3. ORIGINATOR AND BENEFICIARY INFORMATION
3.4 Repeated receipt of incomplete transfers from the same remitting bank, being three or more instances in a calendar month, shall be reported to the HFCC.

4. TRANSACTION THRESHOLDS AND APPROVALS
4.1 A domestic wire transfer by a New Relationship Customer for an amount exceeding Rs. 7,50,000 in a single transaction shall be subject to second-level review by the Branch Operations Manager before release.

4. TRANSACTION THRESHOLDS AND APPROVALS
4.2 The second-level review under clause 4.1 shall be completed within 4 working hours of the transfer request. If the review is not completed within that time, the transfer shall be escalated to the Regional Operations Head.

4. TRANSACTION THRESHOLDS AND APPROVALS
4.3 An outward cross-border remittance exceeding USD 15,000, or its equivalent in any other currency, shall require the prior approval of the HFCC.

4. TRANSACTION THRESHOLDS AND APPROVALS
4.4 Outward cross-border remittances by the same customer that aggregate to more than USD 40,000 within any rolling period of 30 days shall be referred to the HFCC for review, even if no single remittance exceeds the limit in clause 4.3.

4. TRANSACTION THRESHOLDS AND APPROVALS
4.5 The thresholds in this Section 4 do not apply to transfers involving jurisdictions covered by Section 6 or customers covered by Section 7, which are subject to the stricter requirements of those Sections.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.1 Every wire transfer shall be screened, before release, against (a) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (b) the lists notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs under section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, and (c) the Bank's Internal Watchlist.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.2 A screening match with a fuzzy match score of 85 or above shall result in the transfer being placed on hold automatically.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.3 A transfer placed on hold under clause 5.2 may be released only by a Level-2 analyst of the Sanctions Desk, and the decision shall be recorded within 24 hours of the hold.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.4 Where the Level-2 analyst confirms a true match against a list referred to in clause 5.1(a) or 5.1(b), the funds shall be frozen without delay and the matter shall be reported to the Principal Officer within 2 hours of confirmation.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.5 A true match against the Internal Watchlist only shall not by itself result in a freeze, but the transfer shall be treated as a high-risk transaction requiring HFCC approval.

5. SANCTIONS SCREENING
5.6 Screening thresholds and list sources may be changed only with the written approval of the Chief Compliance Officer.

6. HIGH-RISK JURISDICTIONS
6.1 Wire transfers to or from any jurisdiction identified by FATF as a "High-Risk Jurisdiction subject to a Call for Action" are prohibited.

6. HIGH-RISK JURISDICTIONS
6.2 Wire transfers of any amount to or from a jurisdiction identified by FATF as a "Jurisdiction under Increased Monitoring" shall be subject to enhanced due diligence and shall require the prior approval of the HFCC.

6. HIGH-RISK JURISDICTIONS
6.3 The Financial Crime Compliance Department shall update the list of jurisdictions under this Section within 5 working days of each FATF plenary publication.

7. POLITICALLY EXPOSED PERSONS
7.1 Every wire transfer of any amount originated by or received for a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), a family member of a PEP, or a close associate of a PEP shall be subject to enhanced due diligence.

7. POLITICALLY EXPOSED PERSONS
7.2 An outward cross-border remittance by a PEP shall require the prior approval of the Chief Compliance Officer, irrespective of the amount.

7. POLITICALLY EXPOSED PERSONS
7.3 Notwithstanding clause 7.1, domestic salary or pension credits received by a PEP from a government department, for an amount not exceeding Rs. 2,00,000 per month, are exempt from per-transaction enhanced due diligence. Such credits shall instead be reviewed in the annual PEP account review.

8. SUSPICIOUS TRANSACTION ESCALATION
8.1 Any employee who suspects that a wire transfer may involve the proceeds of crime shall raise an internal alert to the Financial Crime Compliance Department within 1 working day of forming the suspicion.

8. SUSPICIOUS TRANSACTION ESCALATION
8.2 The Financial Crime Compliance Department shall complete its investigation of an internal alert and submit its recommendation to the Principal Officer within 2 working days of receiving the alert.

8. SUSPICIOUS TRANSACTION ESCALATION
8.3 The Principal Officer shall decide whether to file a Suspicious Transaction Report with FIU-IND within 5 working days of receiving the recommendation.

8. SUSPICIOUS TRANSACTION ESCALATION
8.4 No employee shall disclose to the customer, or to any other person, that an internal alert has been raised or that a Suspicious Transaction Report is being considered or has been filed.

9. RECORD RETENTION
9.1 Records of all wire transfers, including screening results and the reasons for releasing any held transfer, shall be retained for a period of 8 years from the date of the transaction.

9. RECORD RETENTION
9.2 Where a record relates to a transaction that is the subject of an investigation or a Suspicious Transaction Report, it shall be retained until the investigation is closed or for 8 years, whichever is later.

10. BREACHES AND DISCIPLINARY ACTION
10.1 Releasing a transfer that required an approval under Sections 4, 5, 6 or 7 without obtaining that approval shall be treated as a Category-A breach.

10. BREACHES AND DISCIPLINARY ACTION
10.2 A Category-A breach shall be reported to the Board Risk Committee within 7 days and shall attract disciplinary action under the Bank's Staff Conduct Code, which may include suspension.

10. BREACHES AND DISCIPLINARY ACTION
10.3 A failure to complete a review within the time limits in this SOP, where the transfer was not released, shall be treated as a Category-B breach and recorded in the staff member's annual performance assessment.

ANNEXURE A - SUMMARY OF WIRE TRANSFER APPROVAL LIMITS
Domestic transfer by New Relationship Customer, single transaction above Rs. 7,50,000: Branch Operations Manager review within 4 working hours.
Outward cross-border remittance, single transaction above USD 15,000: HFCC prior approval.
Outward cross-border remittances aggregating above USD 40,000 in rolling 30 days: HFCC review.
Any transfer involving a FATF Increased Monitoring jurisdiction: enhanced due diligence and HFCC prior approval.
Any transfer involving a FATF Call for Action jurisdiction: prohibited.
Outward cross-border remittance by a PEP, any amount: Chief Compliance Officer prior approval.
Sanctions screening hold, match score 85 or above: release only by Sanctions Desk Level-2 analyst within 24 hours.

FACTUALIS BANK LIMITED (FICTIONAL ENTITY - HACKATHON DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT)
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: CUSTOMER DUE DILIGENCE AND RISK CATEGORISATION
Document ID: FB-CDD-SOP | Version 3.0 | Effective date: 01 April 2026
Owner: Financial Crime Compliance Department | Approved by: Board Risk Committee

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This SOP describes how Factualis Bank Limited identifies and verifies its customers, assigns them a money-laundering risk category, and keeps their information up to date.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.2 This SOP applies to individual customers, sole proprietorships, partnership firms and companies that open savings, current or term deposit accounts with the Bank.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.3 This SOP does not cover accounts of minors, accounts of trusts and foundations, or accounts opened for non-resident Indians. Those accounts are governed by the Bank's Special Accounts Policy, which is not part of this SOP.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.4 This SOP shall be read together with the Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016 issued by the Reserve Bank of India. Where this SOP is stricter, this SOP shall prevail.

2. CUSTOMER RISK CATEGORIES
2.1 Every customer shall be assigned one of three risk categories at onboarding: Low, Medium or High.

2. CUSTOMER RISK CATEGORIES
2.2 A customer shall be categorised as High risk if any of the following applies: (a) the customer is a Politically Exposed Person or a family member or close associate of one; (b) the customer's expected annual credit turnover exceeds Rs. 5,00,00,000; (c) the customer has a registered address in a FATF Jurisdiction under Increased Monitoring; (d) the customer is a dealer in precious metals, precious stones or high-value art; or (e) the Financial Crime Compliance Department has directed High risk categorisation.

2. CUSTOMER RISK CATEGORIES
2.3 A customer shall be categorised as Medium risk if the customer is not High risk and either (a) the customer's expected annual credit turnover exceeds Rs. 50,00,000, or (b) the customer is a partnership firm or a company.

2. CUSTOMER RISK CATEGORIES
2.4 All other customers shall be categorised as Low risk.

2. CUSTOMER RISK CATEGORIES
2.5 The risk category assigned by the system may be lowered only with the written approval of the Zonal Compliance Head, and the reason shall be recorded in the customer file.

3. IDENTIFICATION DOCUMENTS
3.1 An individual customer shall submit a Permanent Account Number (PAN) card or Form 60, and one Officially Valid Document for proof of identity and address.

3. IDENTIFICATION DOCUMENTS
3.2 For the purposes of this SOP, the Officially Valid Documents accepted by the Bank are the passport, the driving licence, the proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, and the job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government.

3. IDENTIFICATION DOCUMENTS
3.3 A company shall submit its certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, PAN, a board resolution authorising the account opening, and the identification documents of every beneficial owner.

3. IDENTIFICATION DOCUMENTS
3.4 For a company, a beneficial owner is any natural person who, whether acting alone or together, owns or is entitled to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

3. IDENTIFICATION DOCUMENTS
3.5 For a partnership firm, a beneficial owner is any natural person who owns or is entitled to more than 10 percent of the capital or profits of the partnership.

4. VERIFICATION CHANNELS
4.1 Low risk and Medium risk individual customers may be onboarded through the Bank's Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP).

4. VERIFICATION CHANNELS
4.2 High risk customers shall be onboarded only through in-person verification at a branch, and V-CIP shall not be used for them.

4. VERIFICATION CHANNELS
4.3 A V-CIP session shall be conducted only by an official of the Bank who has completed the V-CIP certification programme, and the session recording shall be retained for 8 years.

4. VERIFICATION CHANNELS
4.4 A V-CIP session shall be terminated and treated as unsuccessful if the customer's live image does not match the photograph on the identification document, or if the session is interrupted for more than 3 minutes.

5. ONBOARDING APPROVALS
5.1 Onboarding of a High risk customer shall require the approval of the Zonal Compliance Head.

5. ONBOARDING APPROVALS
5.2 Onboarding of a Politically Exposed Person shall require the approval of the Chief Compliance Officer. This approval is in addition to, and not a substitute for, the approval required under clause 5.1.

5. ONBOARDING APPROVALS
5.3 Where an existing customer becomes a Politically Exposed Person, the relationship may continue only with the approval of the Chief Compliance Officer obtained within 30 days of the Bank becoming aware of the change.

5. ONBOARDING APPROVALS
5.4 The Bank shall not open an account where it is unable to apply appropriate customer due diligence measures, or where the customer refuses to provide the documents required by Section 3.

6. PERIODIC UPDATION OF KYC
6.1 KYC information shall be updated at least once every 18 months for High risk customers, once every 6 years for Medium risk customers, and once every 9 years for Low risk customers.

6. PERIODIC UPDATION OF KYC
6.2 The period under clause 6.1 shall be counted from the date of account opening or the date of the last KYC updation, whichever is later.

6. PERIODIC UPDATION OF KYC
6.3 Where there is no change in KYC information, a Low risk individual customer may confirm this through a self-declaration submitted through the Bank's internet banking, mobile banking or registered email.

6. PERIODIC UPDATION OF KYC
6.4 If periodic updation is not completed within 90 days after it falls due, the account shall be partially frozen so that debits are not allowed, while credits continue to be allowed.

6. PERIODIC UPDATION OF KYC
6.5 A partial freeze under clause 6.4 shall be removed within 2 working days of the customer completing the KYC updation.

7. CASH TRANSACTION MONITORING
7.1 PAN or Form 60 shall be obtained for every cash deposit of Rs. 50,000 and above in a single transaction.

7. CASH TRANSACTION MONITORING
7.2 Cash deposits into a savings account that aggregate to Rs. 9,00,000 or more in a calendar month shall generate an alert to the Financial Crime Compliance Department.

7. CASH TRANSACTION MONITORING
7.3 Cash deposits into a current account that aggregate to Rs. 25,00,000 or more in a calendar month shall generate an alert to the Financial Crime Compliance Department.

7. CASH TRANSACTION MONITORING
7.4 An alert under clause 7.2 or 7.3 shall be reviewed within 5 working days, and the review outcome shall be recorded in the case management system.

7. CASH TRANSACTION MONITORING
7.5 Splitting of cash deposits by a customer into amounts just below Rs. 50,000 on three or more occasions within 7 days shall be treated as a red flag and reported to the Financial Crime Compliance Department within 1 working day.

8. RECORD KEEPING AND BREACHES
8.1 Customer identification records and the customer file shall be retained for 8 years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.

8. RECORD KEEPING AND BREACHES
8.2 Onboarding a customer without an approval required under Section 5 shall be treated as a Category-A breach under the Bank's Staff Conduct Code.

8. RECORD KEEPING AND BREACHES
8.3 A Category-A breach under this SOP shall attract a monetary penalty of Rs. 25,000 on the approving official, in addition to any disciplinary action.

ANNEXURE A - KYC UPDATION PERIODICITY
High risk customer: at least once every 18 months.
Medium risk customer: at least once every 6 years.
Low risk customer: at least once every 9 years.
Updation overdue by more than 90 days: partial freeze (no debits, credits allowed).

FACTUALIS BANK LIMITED (FICTIONAL ENTITY - HACKATHON DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT)
POLICY: EMPLOYEE PERSONAL DEALING AND INSIDER TRADING CODE OF CONDUCT
Document ID: FB-PERSONAL-DEALING-POLICY | Version 2.2 | Effective date: 01 April 2026
Owner: Compliance Officer (Securities) | Approved by: Board of Directors

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This Policy is the Bank's code of conduct under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. It regulates trading in securities by Designated Persons of the Bank and their immediate relatives.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.2 This Policy applies to trading in the equity shares, debentures and derivatives of Factualis Bank Limited and of any listed company that is a client of the Bank's Corporate Banking or Investment Banking divisions.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.3 This Policy does not cover trading in mutual fund units, sovereign gold bonds, government securities, or crypto assets. Those instruments are not regulated by this Policy.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Designated Person" means every employee in the grade of Assistant Vice President and above, every employee of the Corporate Banking, Investment Banking, Treasury and Finance departments irrespective of grade, and every director of the Bank.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.2 "Compliance Officer (Securities)" means the officer designated by the Board to administer this Policy.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.3 "Restricted List" means the list of listed companies maintained by the Compliance Officer (Securities) in respect of which the Bank holds, or is likely to hold, unpublished price sensitive information.

3. TRADING WINDOW
3.1 The trading window for the securities of Factualis Bank Limited shall be closed from the end of every quarter until 48 hours after the declaration of the financial results for that quarter.

3. TRADING WINDOW
3.2 The trading window may also be closed by the Compliance Officer (Securities) at any other time when Designated Persons are reasonably expected to possess unpublished price sensitive information.

3. TRADING WINDOW
3.3 No Designated Person or immediate relative of a Designated Person shall trade in the Bank's securities while the trading window is closed.

4. PRE-CLEARANCE OF TRADES
4.1 A Designated Person who intends to trade in the Bank's securities, where the value of the proposed trade, whether in one transaction or a series of transactions over a calendar quarter, exceeds Rs. 5,00,000, shall obtain pre-clearance from the Compliance Officer (Securities).

4. PRE-CLEARANCE OF TRADES
4.2 A trade for which pre-clearance has been obtained shall be executed within 5 trading days of the pre-clearance. If it is not executed within that period, fresh pre-clearance shall be obtained.

4. PRE-CLEARANCE OF TRADES
4.3 A Designated Person who is a director of the Bank shall obtain pre-clearance from the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, instead of from the Compliance Officer (Securities), irrespective of the value of the trade.

4. PRE-CLEARANCE OF TRADES
4.4 No pre-clearance shall be given for any trade while the trading window is closed.

5. RESTRICTED LIST
5.1 No Designated Person shall trade in the securities of any company on the Restricted List.

5. RESTRICTED LIST
5.2 Notwithstanding clause 5.1, a Designated Person who does not work in the Corporate Banking or Investment Banking divisions may trade in the securities of a company on the Restricted List with the prior written approval of the Compliance Officer (Securities), where the value of the trade does not exceed Rs. 1,00,000.

6. MINIMUM HOLDING PERIOD
6.1 A Designated Person who buys or sells any number of the Bank's securities shall not execute an opposite transaction during the next 6 months.

6. MINIMUM HOLDING PERIOD
6.2 Where a contra trade is executed in breach of clause 6.1, the profits from such trade shall be disgorged for remittance to the Investor Protection and Education Fund administered by SEBI.

7. DISCLOSURES
7.1 Every Designated Person shall disclose the names and PAN of their immediate relatives, and of persons with whom they share a material financial relationship, within 15 days of becoming a Designated Person and thereafter by 30 April of every year.

7. DISCLOSURES
7.2 Every Designated Person shall report to the Compliance Officer (Securities) every trade in the Bank's securities within 2 trading days of the trade.

8. VIOLATIONS
8.1 A first violation of this Policy shall attract a written warning and a monetary penalty of Rs. 50,000.

8. VIOLATIONS
8.2 A second violation of this Policy within 3 years of the first shall attract suspension from service for a period of up to 6 months, in addition to a monetary penalty of Rs. 2,00,000.

8. VIOLATIONS
8.3 The Compliance Officer (Securities) shall inform SEBI of any violation of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 promptly.
